text: If the push-pull shows flux imbalance (rising magnetizing current, core saturation), verify current sensing is per-switch (not averaged). If leakage inductance causes excessive voltage spikes, add snubbers or consider an active clamp. For higher power (>500W), consider half-bridge or full-bridge.

title: SEPIC Converter Strategy
text: SEPIC has an RHPZ in CCM at f_RHPZ = R*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L1). Prefer cascaded current-inner voltage-outer control. The inner loop regulates L1 current; the outer loop regulates output voltage. Single-loop PI is feasible only in DCM.

title: SEPIC Converter Strategy
text: CCM/DCM boundary: R_crit = (1-D)*fsw*2*L1/D^2. RHPZ: f_RHPZ = R*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L1). Voltage-loop crossover: f_c < f_RHPZ/4. Coupling capacitor C1 must handle RMS current: I_C1_rms = I_out * sqrt(D/(1-D)).

title: SEPIC Converter Strategy
text: The SEPIC RHPZ frequency drops at high duty cycle and light load, limiting bandwidth. At D approaching 1, f_RHPZ becomes very low. The coupling capacitor C1 voltage equals V_in, so its rating must match the input voltage range.

title: SEPIC Converter Strategy
text: If the SEPIC cannot meet transient specs because the RHPZ frequency is below the required bandwidth, consider: (1) operating in DCM to eliminate RHPZ (at the cost of higher ripple), (2) interleaved SEPIC, or (3) a different topology like buck-boost if isolation is not required.

title: Series Resonant Converter Strategy
text: Use SRC for applications with relatively constant load. SRC has no parallel inductor — gain is always <= 1 and strongly load-dependent. Control range is narrower than LLC. Best when the load is predictable and the conversion ratio is modest.

title: Series Resonant Converter Strategy
text: SRC gain decreases monotonically with frequency above resonance. At light load, the gain curve is very flat and the converter loses regulation ability. LLC is preferred when wide load range regulation is needed.

title: Series Resonant Converter Strategy
text: Same as LLC: PI controller with kp in Hz/V and ki in Hz/(V*s). The output is a switching frequency command. Operate above resonance for ZVS. Frequency range is narrower than LLC — typically 0.9*fr to 1.3*fr.

title: Vienna Rectifier Strategy
text: Use Vienna rectifier for three-phase unidirectional PFC. Only three active switches (vs six in conventional bridge), inherent three-level modulation reduces input current THD, no shoot-through risk. THD < 5% achievable with proper current-loop bandwidth.

title: Vienna Rectifier Strategy
text: Control in dq frame with inner current loop and outer voltage loop. Neutral-point voltage balance is an additional control loop that adjusts the common-mode duty-cycle offset. The voltage loop bandwidth must stay below 2*f_line (typically 10-20 Hz).

title: Vienna Rectifier Strategy
text: Unidirectional power flow only (boost mode). Neutral-point voltage balancing is required — if the split capacitors have unequal voltage, the output current waveform distorts. The neutral-point balancing loop should be 5-10x faster than the voltage loop.

title: Vienna Rectifier Strategy
text: If THD is high, increase current-loop bandwidth. If the neutral-point voltage oscillates, increase the balancing loop gain. If the output voltage oscillates at 6*f_line, reduce the voltage-loop bandwidth below 2*f_line.

title: Bidirectional DC-DC Dual-Loop Tuning Rules
text: Tune the current loop with identical gains in both directions of power flow. Asymmetric gains create different small-signal margins in charge versus discharge, which shows up as direction-dependent settling time and is hard to diagnose from a single test condition.

title: Bidirectional DC-DC Dual-Loop Tuning Rules
text: At a sign change in the current reference, the inner integrator must be reset or held rather than carried across, otherwise the controller stalls on the wrong side of zero for several time constants. This is the single most common failure on bidirectional designs and is invisible to step-response tests that stay on one side of zero.

title: Bidirectional DC-DC Dual-Loop Tuning Rules
text: Buck-side voltage regulation and boost-side voltage regulation involve different small-signal plants. Schedule the outer-loop gains by direction if a single fixed set of gains fails to meet both transient targets. If gain scheduling is not available, design at the worst case (boost direction in CCM, where the RHPZ caps bandwidth).

title: Bidirectional DC-DC Dual-Loop Tuning Rules
text: When the load side is a battery, the load is not a pure resistance — battery impedance has frequency dependence and large open-circuit voltage drift. Avoid integrators that try to regulate against the battery's terminal voltage at low frequency; use a current set-point loop instead and let an outer SOC/voltage manager set the reference.

title: Boost Average Current Mode Tuning Rules
text: Tune the inner current loop first and keep the outer voltage loop well below the right-half-plane-zero frequency so the voltage regulator does not fight the boost power-stage limitation.

title: Boost Average Current Mode Tuning Rules
text: If the response is too slow but stable, first improve current-loop tracking and only then increase outer voltage-loop aggressiveness.

title: Buck-Boost Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: The small-signal control-to-output gain of a buck-boost varies strongly with duty cycle. If the input range is wide, design the voltage-loop gain at the worst-case operating point (maximum duty, minimum input) and verify margin at the boost extreme rather than the buck extreme.

title: Buck-Boost Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: In CCM boost-mode operation, a buck-boost exhibits a right-half-plane zero whose frequency scales with load current and (1 - D)^2. Place the voltage-loop crossover at least a factor of 3 below the worst-case RHPZ frequency; chasing higher bandwidth produces non-minimum-phase undershoot that no inner current loop can hide.

title: Buck-Boost Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Set the inner current-loop crossover roughly fsw/10 in CCM. In DCM the small-signal current dynamics collapse to a single pole and the current loop can be made much faster, but verify the mode boundary explicitly — switching between CCM and DCM mid-transient is a frequent source of evaluation failures.

title: Buck-Boost Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Inverting buck-boost topologies require careful sign tracking in both sensor scaling and controller output. A polarity error here is indistinguishable in early simulation from an under-tuned controller — verify open-loop step response polarity before tightening gains.

title: Buck Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Tune the current inner loop substantially faster than the voltage outer loop so that the outer loop sees a well-regulated current actuator. This separation is the main reason cascaded control improves transient response.

title: Buck Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: When the design has already failed multiple transient checks, prefer changing loop structure before pushing gains to aggressive values that may hurt efficiency or robustness.

title: Buck PI Tuning Rules
text: A practical digital voltage-loop PI implementation for a buck converter often uses a sample time faster than the switching period subdivision already exposed by the control pipeline. Avoid selecting a sample time slower than the dominant output dynamics.

title: Buck PI Tuning Rules
text: If the response is too sluggish and stable, increase proportional gain first, then integral gain. If overshoot rises sharply, back off proportional gain or add current-loop structure instead of only raising integral gain.

title: CLLC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: kp ~ fr/Vout (Hz/V), ki ~ fr/(5*Vout) (Hz/(V*s)). CLLC is symmetric, so the gain curve is the same for forward and reverse power flow.

title: CLLC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: For bidirectional operation, the same PI gains should work in both directions because the CLLC tank is symmetric. Verify stability at both forward and reverse power flow. The bridge role switching adds latency — account for this in the bandwidth.

title: CLLC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: sample time <= 1/(10*fsw_max). For a 200 kHz CLLC, sample at <= 5 us.

title: Cuk Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Sense L2 (output inductor) current for the inner loop — this gives direct control of the output dynamics. Bandwidth: f_ci ~ fsw/5 to fsw/10. PI compensator. The inverted output requires sign-inverted feedback or a negative reference in the controller.

title: Cuk Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: f_cv < f_RHPZ/4 where f_RHPZ = (1-D)^2*R/(2*pi*L2). Design for worst case: minimum R (max load), maximum D. Start with kp = 2*pi*f_cv*C_out and ki = kp * f_cv / 5. The integrator must be anti-windup clamped because the duty cycle saturates at 0 and 1.

title: Cuk Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: If the Cuk oscillates at fsw/2, this is subharmonic instability from peak-current-mode — add slope compensation >= inductor downslope / 2. If it cannot meet transient specs in CCM, consider DCM operation or a different topology.

title: DAB Phase-Shift Control Tuning
text: The relationship between phase shift and power is nonlinear (sinusoidal). Near phi=0, the sensitivity dP/dphi is low. Near phi=pi/2, sensitivity is high. The PI controller must handle this gain variation across the operating range.

title: DAB Phase-Shift Control Tuning
text: Set the voltage-loop crossover at fsw/20 to fsw/10. The plant is essentially a first-order system (L filters the power transfer), so a simple PI works well. Start with kp ~ 2*pi*f_crossover*L_series/Vout.

title: DAB Phase-Shift Control Tuning
text: When the power reference crosses zero, the phase-shift command must cross zero smoothly. Anti-windup reset at phi=0 prevents the integrator from stalling on the wrong side. Implement a dead-band around phi=0 to prevent chattering.

title: DAB Phase-Shift Control Tuning
text: Increasing kp improves transient response but may cause phase-shift overshoot (the output oscillates around the target). If the phase-shift command oscillates, reduce kp. For steady-state error, increase ki — but watch for integrator windup at the phase-shift limits.

title: Flyback Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Peak current-mode flyback operating above 50% duty in CCM is subharmonically unstable without slope compensation. Add an artificial ramp with slope at least half of the inductor down-slope reflected to the primary. Insufficient slope compensation appears as period-doubling on the current waveform, which evaluators may misread as a tuning problem.

title: Flyback Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Place the outer voltage-loop crossover at approximately fsw/10 to fsw/5 in DCM. In CCM, the right-half-plane zero — frequency proportional to load and (1 - D)^2 — typically caps voltage-loop crossover at one quarter of the RHPZ frequency.

title: Flyback Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Primary leakage inductance produces a voltage spike that is sensed alongside the legitimate switch current. If the controller acts on the spike, the duty-cycle command oscillates. Apply leading-edge blanking on the current sense long enough to clear the leakage transient before the loop sees it.

title: Flyback Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: DCM-to-CCM transition changes the small-signal model from a single-pole system to a double-pole-plus-RHPZ system. Pick the operating-point worst case (typically heavy load in CCM) for stability margin verification, and accept that DCM small-signal margin will be much larger.

title: Forward Converter Cascaded Control Tuning
text: Inner current loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. Outer voltage loop crossover: f_cv ~ f_ci/5 to f_ci/3. This ensures the current loop settles before the voltage loop acts. The current loop handles the fast inductor dynamics.

title: Forward Converter Cascaded Control Tuning
text: For the current loop: increase kp until the current tracks the reference within one switching cycle, then add ki for zero steady-state error. For the voltage loop: increase kp for faster transient response, increase ki for lower steady-state voltage error.

title: Forward Converter Cascaded Control Tuning
text: If D > 0.5 at any operating point, add slope compensation with ramp slope >= inductor downslope / 2. Without it, subharmonic instability occurs near fsw/2. The ramp is added to the current sense signal.

title: Forward Converter Cascaded Control Tuning
text: Current loop sample time: <= 1/(10*fsw). Voltage loop sample time: can be slower, <= 1/(5*fsw). The current loop needs faster sampling to catch the peak current accurately.

title: Forward Converter Cascaded Control Tuning
text: The plant gain varies with input voltage (D changes with Vin). At maximum Vin, D is smallest and the plant gain is lowest. Verify current-loop stability at both Vin_min and Vin_max.

title: Full-Bridge Isolated Cascaded Control Tuning
text: Inner current loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. Outer voltage loop crossover: f_cv ~ f_ci/5 to f_ci/3. Same bandwidth ordering as forward converter. The current loop handles the primary-side inductor dynamics.

title: Full-Bridge Isolated Cascaded Control Tuning
text: For the current loop: increase kp until the primary current tracks within one switching cycle. For the voltage loop: increase kp for transient response, increase ki for steady-state accuracy. Full-bridge allows higher duty cycle than forward, so the gain range is wider.

title: Full-Bridge Isolated Cascaded Control Tuning
text: Full-bridge can operate at D > 0.5, so slope compensation is mandatory. Ramp slope >= inductor downslope / 2. The slope compensation affects the current-loop gain — account for it in the loop design.

title: Full-Bridge Isolated Cascaded Control Tuning
text: The plant gain varies with input voltage and load. At light load, the LC filter is more resonant (higher Q). Verify voltage-loop stability at both full load and light load. At Vin_max, the duty cycle is smallest and the current-loop gain is lowest.

title: Half-Bridge Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Per-switch peak-current sensing with leading-edge blanking (100-300ns). Current-loop bandwidth: f_ci ~ fsw/5. Slope compensation: ramp >= V_out*N_pri/N_sec / (2*L_out*fsw). The split-capacitor midpoint drifts if current sensing is asymmetric.

title: Half-Bridge Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Output ripple frequency = 2*fsw. Voltage-loop crossover: f_cv ~ 2*fsw/10 to 2*fsw/20. PI compensator. The split-capacitor midpoint voltage should be monitored — if it drifts more than 5% from V_in/2, the current sensing or duty cycle is asymmetric.

title: Half-Bridge Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: If the half-bridge shows split-capacitor midpoint drift, verify: (1) per-switch current sensing (not averaged), (2) equal blanking times, (3) symmetric gate drive. If leakage inductance causes voltage spikes, add an RCD snubber or active clamp.

title: Single-Phase Inverter PR (Proportional-Resonant) Tuning Rules
text: Place the resonant pole exactly at the output fundamental (50 or 60 Hz, or the islanded reference frequency). Even small offset produces a steady-state phase error that no proportional term recovers. If the system must track grid frequency, make the resonant frequency a function of the measured grid frequency rather than a fixed constant.

title: Single-Phase Inverter PR (Proportional-Resonant) Tuning Rules
text: An ideal PR controller has infinite gain at the resonant frequency, which is unrealizable on a digital implementation. Use a damped form (k_r * 2*ω_c*s / (s^2 + 2*ω_c*s + ω_0^2)) and start with ω_c ≈ 5 to 10 rad/s. Lower damping gives better tracking but reduces the system phase margin near ω_0.

title: Single-Phase Inverter PR (Proportional-Resonant) Tuning Rules
text: For nonlinear loads, add resonant compensators at the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics, each with its own damping. Tune each compensator gain individually — combined gain is not a simple sum because the harmonics interact through the load current. Add them one at a time and verify margin after each.

title: Single-Phase Inverter PR (Proportional-Resonant) Tuning Rules
text: PR controllers are sensitive to discretization method. Bilinear (Tustin) with prewarping at the resonant frequency preserves the pole location best. Forward or backward Euler shifts the resonant pole and introduces a steady-state error proportional to the sample time.

title: Single-Phase Inverter PR (Proportional-Resonant) Tuning Rules
text: Use a sample time at least 20x faster than the highest compensated harmonic. For 7th harmonic compensation on 60 Hz, sample at >= 8.4 kHz. Below this, the resonant poles alias and the controller can become unstable.

title: Inverter dq Tuning Rules
text: For dq control, tune the current loop before the outer voltage or power loop. The inner loop should dominate dynamic response and operate at the fastest practical sample time available in the switching workflow.

title: LCL Inverter Active Damping Tuning Rules
text: Establish damping or resonance attenuation before pushing current-loop crossover. Without that ordering, a faster dq controller can excite the LCL pole pair instead of improving tracking.

title: LCL Inverter Active Damping Tuning Rules
text: Keep sensing and PWM delay in mind because digital delay reduces the practical damping margin of LCL-filtered current control.

title: Three-Phase Inverter AHO-Based VOC Tuning Rules
text: Tune oscillator amplitude restoration conservatively so the oscillator state converges smoothly before any outer voltage-restoration action becomes aggressive.

title: Three-Phase Inverter AHO-Based VOC Tuning Rules
text: Keep the current-protection or current-inner loop faster than the oscillator envelope dynamics so current limiting clips or bounds the commanded waveform without destabilizing the oscillator.

title: Three-Phase Inverter AHO-Based VOC Tuning Rules
text: In weak-grid mode, prefer modest oscillator forcing and damping values before increasing voltage-restoration gain, and avoid making oscillator frequency fully dependent on a fixed external angle source.

title: Inverter VSG Tuning Rules
text: For VSG control, use conservative gains and preserve clear time-scale separation between virtual machine dynamics and current regulation. Overly aggressive gains can amplify weak-grid oscillation risk.

title: LCC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: kp ~ fr/Vout (Hz/V), ki ~ fr/(5*Vout) (Hz/(V*s)). The LCC gain curve depends on the Cp/Cr ratio. Higher Cp makes the gain curve flatter, requiring higher gains.

title: LCC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: increase kp for faster response, reduce kp if frequency oscillates. LCC has a wider control range than SRC but narrower than LLC for the same tank parameters.

title: LCC Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: sample time <= 1/(10*fsw_max). For a 200 kHz LCC, sample at <= 5 us.

title: LLC Resonant Converter Frequency Control Tuning
text: kp is in Hz/V. Start with kp ~ fr/Vout. ki is in Hz/(V*s). Start with ki ~ fr/(5*Vout). These are starting points; actual values depend heavily on tank parameters and operating point.

title: LLC Resonant Converter Frequency Control Tuning
text: Increasing kp speeds up the response but can cause frequency overshoot (output oscillates around the resonant point). If the frequency command oscillates, reduce kp first. If the response is sluggish but stable, increase kp then ki.

title: LLC Resonant Converter Frequency Control Tuning
text: At light load, the plant gain (Vout/Hz) is very small, so the PI needs high gains. At heavy load, the plant gain is large, so the PI needs lower gains. If a single gain set cannot work across the load range, consider gain scheduling by load current.

title: LLC Resonant Converter Frequency Control Tuning
text: The switching frequency for LLC is typically 50-500 kHz. The control sample time should be at least 10x faster than the maximum switching frequency. For a 200 kHz LLC, sample at <= 5 us.

title: LLC Resonant Converter Frequency Control Tuning
text: Start with a high switching frequency (low gain) and ramp down to the target frequency. This prevents excessive inrush current through the resonant tank at startup. Do not step the frequency command directly to the target.

title: NPC Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: Dq-frame PI current controller. Crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. Include dq decoupling: Vd_ff = -omega*L*Iq, Vq_ff = omega*L*Id. For LCL filter, add active damping via capacitor-current feedback gain R_d ~ 1/(3*Cf*omega_res).

title: NPC Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: DC-bus voltage PI controller. Crossover: f_cv ~ f_ci/10 ~ fsw/100. The voltage loop output sets the d-axis current reference. Anti-windup is critical because the current reference saturates.

title: NPC Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: Separate slow loop that adjusts zero-vector dwell time. Bandwidth ~ f_ci/10. If balancing oscillates, reduce the gain. If it cannot converge, the DC-bus capacitors may be too small or the load is too unbalanced.

title: Boost PFC Average Current Mode Tuning
text: Average-current-mode inner loop shapes the input current to follow the rectified line voltage reference. Crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. The current compensator is typically Type II (PI with lead) to cancel the boost inductor pole. The current reference is the multiplier output: V_err * |V_line|.

title: Boost PFC Average Current Mode Tuning
text: The voltage loop must be very slow to avoid distorting the current reference. Crossover: f_cv ~ 10-20Hz (well below 2*f_line). PI compensator with very low kp and ki. The 2*f_line ripple on the DC bus must not appear in the current reference — the low bandwidth naturally attenuates it.

title: Boost PFC Average Current Mode Tuning
text: If input current THD is high, check: (1) voltage-loop bandwidth is low enough, (2) feedforward of line voltage is accurate, (3) current-loop gain is sufficient at the line frequency. The current loop must track a 50/60Hz sinusoidal reference — it needs adequate bandwidth at the line frequency.

title: PFC Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Set the outer voltage-loop crossover well below twice the line frequency — typically 10 to 20 Hz for 50/60 Hz mains. A higher voltage-loop bandwidth distorts the current reference by passing the 100/120 Hz bulk-capacitor ripple into the inner loop, ruining input THD.

title: PFC Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Adding a notch or low-pass filter on the voltage-loop error at 2×f_line lets the loop tolerate the unavoidable bus ripple without distorting the current reference. Sizing the notch is more effective than dropping the loop bandwidth aggressively low — the latter hurts transient recovery on load steps.

title: PFC Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: Place the inner current-loop crossover near fsw/10 so the line-current waveform tracks the rectified sine reference with negligible phase shift. A current loop slower than line frequency / 100 will cause leading or lagging current distortion that registers as poor power factor regardless of THD.

title: PFC Current-Mode Tuning Rules
text: PFC inrush limiting is rarely solved by the current loop alone. Verify the soft-start ramps the current reference rather than the duty, and that the bulk-cap pre-charge path is sized to avoid hitting the current limit during startup. Loop tuning cannot save a missing pre-charge resistor.

title: Totem-Pole PFC Current Mode Tuning
text: Inner current loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10 to fsw/5. Outer voltage loop crossover: f_cv = 10-20 Hz (must stay below 2*f_line). The voltage loop must be slow enough to not distort the sinusoidal current reference.

title: Totem-Pole PFC Current Mode Tuning
text: The current loop tracks a sinusoidal reference. The plant is a boost inductor with variable duty cycle. Set kp for the desired crossover frequency: kp ~ 2*pi*f_ci*L_boost/Vout. Add ki for zero steady-state error at the line frequency.

title: Totem-Pole PFC Current Mode Tuning
text: The voltage loop regulates the bulk capacitor. kp ~ 2*pi*f_cv*C_bulk/Vout. ki ~ kp*f_cv/5. The voltage loop output is the current amplitude — it multiplies with the rectified line voltage shape to generate the current reference.

title: Totem-Pole PFC Current Mode Tuning
text: If THD is high, increase current-loop bandwidth. If the current loop is too slow, the current waveform distorts at the zero crossings of the line voltage. The current-loop phase margin at 2*f_line determines the power factor.

title: Phase-Shifted Full Bridge Cascaded Control Tuning
text: Inner current loop crossover: f_ci ~ fsw/10. Outer voltage loop crossover: f_cv ~ f_ci/5 to f_ci/3. The current loop controls the primary inductor current; the voltage loop regulates the output.

title: Phase-Shifted Full Bridge Cascaded Control Tuning
text: The effective secondary duty cycle is less than the primary due to the phase-shift overlap. Account for this loss in the gain calculations: D_eff = D_pri - D_loss where D_loss depends on the leakage inductance and load current.

title: Phase-Shifted Full Bridge Cascaded Control Tuning
text: ZVS is maintained by the leakage inductance energy. At light load, the leakage energy may be insufficient for ZVS. The controller cannot fix this — it is a hardware limitation. If ZVS is lost at the operating point, efficiency drops.

title: Phase-Shifted Full Bridge Cascaded Control Tuning
text: For the current loop: increase kp until the current tracks within one switching cycle. For the voltage loop: increase kp for transient response, increase ki for steady-state accuracy. Watch for instability near the ZVS boundary where the plant characteristics change.

title: Push-Pull Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Use per-switch peak-current sensing (one CT per primary switch). The current loop must be fast enough to prevent flux imbalance: f_ci ~ fsw/5. Add slope compensation with ramp >= V_out*N_pri/N_sec / (2*L_out*fsw) to prevent subharmonic oscillation at D approaching 0.5.

title: Push-Pull Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Effective output ripple frequency is 2*fsw, so the voltage loop can run at f_cv ~ 2*fsw/10 to 2*fsw/20. PI compensator. Start with kp = 2*pi*f_cv*C_out / (V_out * 0.01) and ki = kp * f_cv / 10.

title: Push-Pull Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: If the push-pull shows rising magnetizing current (visible as asymmetric primary current), the flux-balance is broken. Verify: (1) current sensing is per-switch, not averaged, (2) slope compensation is equal on both phases, (3) the duty cycle stays below 0.5.

title: SEPIC Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: Sense L1 current for the inner loop. Bandwidth: f_ci ~ fsw/5 to fsw/10. The current loop compensator is typically PI. At light load the RHPZ drops, so the current loop must also slow down — use gain scheduling or keep the current loop bandwidth well below f_RHPZ.

title: SEPIC Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: The voltage-loop crossover must satisfy f_cv < f_RHPZ/4. Since f_RHPZ = R*(1-D)^2/(2*pi*L1), at maximum load (minimum R) and high duty cycle, f_RHPZ is lowest. Design for the worst case. Start with kp = 2*pi*f_cv*C_out and ki = kp * f_cv / 5.

title: SEPIC Cascaded Tuning Rules
text: If the SEPIC fails transient specs in CCM, first check if the RHPZ frequency is above the required bandwidth. If not, operating in DCM (discontinuous current through L1) eliminates the RHPZ at the cost of higher ripple current.

title: Series Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: kp ~ fr/Vout (Hz/V), ki ~ fr/(5*Vout) (Hz/(V*s)). SRC gain curve is steeper than LLC at light load, so gains may need to be higher. At heavy load, gains should be lower.

title: Series Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Increasing kp speeds up response but can cause frequency overshoot. If the frequency command oscillates, reduce kp. SRC has narrower control range than LLC — verify the frequency range covers the required input voltage range.

title: Series Resonant Converter Tuning
text: Same as LLC: sample time <= 1/(10*fsw_max). For a 200 kHz SRC, sample at <= 5 us.

title: T-Type Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: Identical to NPC: dq-frame PI, crossover f_ci ~ fsw/10, dq decoupling, active damping for LCL filter. The T-type has different loss distribution (bidirectional switches carry more current during zero-level) but the control structure is the same.

title: T-Type Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: DC-bus PI controller. Crossover f_cv ~ fsw/100. Anti-windup on current reference saturation. The voltage loop design is identical to NPC.

title: T-Type Three-Level DQ Tuning Rules
text: Same balancing algorithm as NPC. The bidirectional neutral-point switches carry the balancing current — their current rating limits the balancing capability. Reduce balancing gain if the switches are thermally stressed.

title: Vienna Rectifier dq-Frame Tuning
text: Inner current loop (dq): f_ci ~ fsw/10. Neutral-point balancing loop: f_np ~ 5-10x faster than the voltage loop. Outer voltage loop: f_cv = 10-20 Hz (below 2*f_line for three-phase, i.e., below ~120 Hz for 50 Hz grid).

title: Vienna Rectifier dq-Frame Tuning
text: The dq current loops are decoupled with feedforward. Set kp for the desired crossover: kp ~ 2*pi*f_ci*L_boost/Vdc. The d-axis and q-axis plants are identical after decoupling. Add ki for zero steady-state error.

title: Vienna Rectifier dq-Frame Tuning
text: The neutral-point voltage balance loop adjusts the common-mode duty-cycle offset. Gain should be high enough to correct imbalance within 10-20 line cycles. Too high gain causes audible noise from the capacitors.

title: Vienna Rectifier dq-Frame Tuning
text: The voltage loop regulates the total DC-link voltage. kp ~ 2*pi*f_cv*C_dc/Vdc. ki ~ kp*f_cv/5. The voltage loop output is the current amplitude reference for the d-axis current loop.
